import os
base = "https://github.com/Nerlant/review-link-repro/blob/" + "0"*40 + "/"
anchor = "#L1-L3"
paths = {103: "a1.txt", 104: "a12.txt"}
for n in (149, 150, 151, 152):
    name_len = n - len(base) - len(anchor) - len("fixtures/") - len(".txt")
    stem = f"url-{n}-chars-"
    paths[n] = "fixtures/" + stem + "x" * (name_len - len(stem)) + ".txt"
os.makedirs("fixtures", exist_ok=True)
for n, p in sorted(paths.items()):
    url = base + p + anchor
    assert len(url) == n, (n, len(url))
    with open(p, "w") as f:
        f.write(f"Fixture file {p}\nIts blob URL at a full commit SHA with {anchor} is exactly {n} characters long.\nLine 3.\n")
    print(n, p)
EOF

# review-link-repro

Public reproduction of Markdown links being rewritten when a Claude Code cloud
session (claude.ai/code) posts pull request review comments through the GitHub
MCP tools. See the pull request in this repository and `logs/` for the exact
tool calls, inputs and stored results.

The files in `fixtures/` and the two `a*.txt` files exist only so that their
blob URLs at a full 40-character commit SHA have exact lengths (103, 104, 149,
150, 151 and 152 characters, including a `#L1-L3` anchor).
EOF
